statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-11564: an easy handle that first uses the default native CA trust can keep trusting the native platform store after the application switches the same handle to custom CA material, through connection reuse. curl 8.17.0 to 8.20.0 are affected; 8.21.0 is not (also 8.20.1 on the 8.20 branch): https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-11564.html. curl notes that the flaw applies to builds that use the native CA store by default, an option on Apple and Windows platforms; the status here follows the release boundary. The fix, https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/d69bfad3fa3daf5e72331f6870667607828d5891, is in the curl-8_21_0 release tag and not in curl-8_20_0. This owner's Alpine 3.23 builds are 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1. On x86_64 and aarch64, the libcurl library and the curl program in each report the curl release of the package version. Builds 8.17.0-r1 to 8.20.0-r1 package curl 8.17.0 to 8.20.0 without the fix (8.20.0-r1 is a rebuild of curl 8.20.0 that adds no patch) and are affected; 8.21.0-r0 and later package curl 8.21.0 or newer, which contain it. Alpine's 3.23-stable curl APKBUILD lists this CVE under its 8.22.0-r0 secfixes (https://gitlab.alpinelinux.org/alpine/aports/-/blob/3.23-stable/main/curl/APKBUILD); this owner's own 8.21.0-r0 build already ships the fixed upstream release. The range ends at 8.21.0-r0.
